source.title: TIDE : Temporal-Aware Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretable Diffusion Transformers in Image Generation
source.authors: Victor Shea-Jay Huang; Le Zhuo; Yi Xin; Zhaokai Wang; Fu-Yun Wang; Yuchi Wang; Ren-Rui Zhang; Peng Gao; Hongsheng Li

record.file_problem: Main paper text is present, but it contains ellipses and refers to supplementary material that is not included.
record.tranche_reason: The study replaces DiT activations with SAE/TIDE reconstructions and measures downstream diffusion loss, a different-method test of whether reconstruction errors affect model computation. It does not compare against random errors of the same size.
record.gate_note: The study reports aggregate SAE reconstruction metrics and a downstream diffusion-loss comparison. It does not analyze linear predictability of residuals, per-token error norms, context overlap across SAE sizes, or a matched random-error baseline. The random-error comparison is essential to V3, so the reported loss cannot establish whether SAE errors are more pathological than random errors.
record.test_reason: The study builds TopK SAEs (TIDE) for diffusion transformers and reports its own method's reconstruction and splicing performance against other SAEs. It never analyses the SAE error vector: no linear prediction of residuals, no per-token error norms, no random-error baseline, and no error-term ablation in circuits or steering. Its spliced diffusion-loss and FID results show only that reconstructions cost something. V3 needs a comparison with same-size random errors to say the error is pathological. Architecture comparisons rank SAE variants by quality but do not decompose dark matter, so they do not bear on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right, but incomplete. The authors' main conclusion is that TIDE, a timestep-aware TopK SAE, extracts interpretable multi-level features (3D, class, semantic) from DiTs. They say it enables editing and safety applications with minimal loss of generation quality (small FID increases). They also state that spliced diffusion loss is comparable to the original model and better than other SAEs. They note that sparsity constraints limit complex editing.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses its own TopK SAE with timestep-dependent modulation, token sampling, and a TIDE architecture; it does not reproduce a dark-matter residual analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction outcomes vary with token sampling and temporal-aware architecture; reported reconstruction also improves with larger latent dimension and higher top-k selection.

fits_no_version.finding: Splicing SAE/TIDE reconstructions into DiTs raises FID modestly. PixArt: baseline 7.30, SAE 7.93, TIDE 7.45. SDXL: 8.24, SAE 8.44, TIDE 8.38. FLUX: 10.09, SAE 10.18, TIDE 10.13. The cost depends strongly on layer: block 4 +3.19, block 27 +0.34, block 28 +0.04. Temporal-aware modulation and larger latent size reduce the degradation. No random-error control is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In diffusion transformers, replacing activations with SAE reconstructions degrades generation quality by a layer-dependent amount; early layers cost more, and timestep-aware SAEs cost less.

record.problems: The downstream diffusion-loss result is shown only in a figure and described qualitatively. No matched-size random-error control is reported, and the supplied text omits supplementary material.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results were entered: the aggregate MSE and cosine-similarity results concern overall reconstruction quality, not the residual properties or matched-error behavior specified by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Whether the SAE error is linearly predictable from the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability, whether larger SAEs fail on the same contexts, and whether error persists with scale. The study shows only that aggregate MSE falls with latent size.
Whether spliced SAE error harms loss more than random error of equal norm. No such baseline is reported.
Splitting the error into linear and nonlinear parts, and their properties.
Whether circuit or steering analyses lose behaviour without the error term.
Whether dark matter is a training artifact. Architecture and sampling changes reduce aggregate MSE, but dark matter is not decomposed.

record.verdict_notes: The study does not analyse dark matter. Table 2 FID deltas and Table 1 MSE/cosine values describe the method's performance, not properties of the SAE residual. The record's V3 link is not warranted, because the random-error comparison central to V3 is absent.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of the SAE error vector is a linear function of the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, whether larger SAEs fail on the same contexts, and whether error persists with scale.
The study measures diffusion loss after SAE reconstruction replaces original activations, but does not compare with random errors of the same size.
The study does not separate linear and nonlinear error components or test their feature-learning properties.
The study does not test whether circuits or steering analyses lose behavior without the error term.
The study varies SAE training strategies and architecture but does not test whether dark matter is primarily a training artifact or whether it shrinks under better objectives or end-to-end training.

conditions.value: activation layers reconstructed by TIDE; specific layer not stated

rows.value: figure only; described as comparable to the original model
rows.locator: Scaling Laws and Downstream Loss of TIDEs; Fig. 4(c)(d)
rows.note: The text also says TIDE surpasses other types of SAEs, but gives no numerical values here. No random-error comparison is reported, so this result cannot determine V3's matched-error prediction.
rows.check: This row compares the study's own method (TIDE) with other SAEs on spliced diffusion loss. It is shown only in Fig. 4(c)(d) and described as comparable to the original model. There is no random-error control of matched norm, so it cannot bear on V3's claim about pathological errors. It should not be linked to V3.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
